- For streaming sessions, are intermediate token fragments kept anywhere?

Hi Alex — thanks for sending this over. Summary below; attaching a concise one‑page retention summary for your reviewers (retention_summary_20281105.pdf). If you want, we can turn this into a short appendix for your questionnaire.

Short answers (hosted API default):
- Default capture: Requests (full user input) and final model responses (completed answers) are captured and retained for 60 days by default.
- Prompts vs derivatives: Original user prompts are treated as part of the request record and follow the 60‑day window for operational logs; derivative persistent artifacts (indexed embeddings, exported files) are retained for up to 365 days unless customer configures otherwise.
- Streaming fragments: Intermediate token buffers and KV‑cache snapshots are ephemeral. By default streaming fragments are kept only in memory and are flushed at session end; transient buffers can exist for up to 12 hours for continuity but are not written to persistent logs unless the client explicitly finalizes the session.
- Erasure SLA & evidence: Standard hosted erasure requests are actioned within 48–72 hours. We provide a signed deletion receipt (timestamp + internal deletion run IDs) and optional export of the deletion audit trail on request.

Notes & configuration options:
- Customers can opt out of request/response capture at request time by sending the header "Redwood-No-Store: true" (API level). This prevents storage of the request/response record for hosted API calls.
- Dedicated and Private deployments: retention windows are configurable by the customer and can be set to 0 days for full erase-on-write behaviour in Private deployments (subject to contractual terms).
- Residency: by default logs live in the region of the customer's workspace (we honor EU vs US residency for hosted workspaces). If you need an export for evidence or e‑discovery we can provide region‑tagged export files.

Alex / team — quick legal note to accompany Mina's technical summary: 
- We distinguish operational telemetry (service metrics, anonymized error traces) from customer content (requests/outputs). Our deletion SLA above applies to customer content artifacts; operational telemetry used for platform health is retained according to our platform telemetry policy and is not returned in erasure exports.
- For procurement: if BrightBank requires shorter default retention (e.g., 30 days) on hosted we can accommodate via a contract addendum for your workspace; for Dedicated/Private we will include configuration guidance and the appropriate Change Order.
- Please let us know if you need proof-of-deletion in a particular format (PDF certificate, signed JSON receipt, or CSV audit export).

Hi Alex — technical clarifications: 
- API erasure endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/customers/{customer_id}/erase with request id and scope (requests, outputs, derivatives). The endpoint returns a job id; deletion is performed async and we include the job id in the signed deletion receipt.
- No-Store header behaviour: Redwood-No-Store: true is honored for the standard HTTP REST endpoints and for the streaming websocket protocol if included in the session-init message. When used on streaming sessions it prevents finalized session artifacts from being written to persistent storage. Note: if an application takes an explicit snapshot (e.g., call to ExportSession) that snapshot will be persisted and follow the normal retention window unless erased.
- Edge cases: partial writes from third‑party connectors (S3 exports, custom sinks) are outside the default hosted retention and must be managed via the connector configuration. We provide guidance and scripts for BrightBank's S3 exports if you plan to auto‑archive outputs.

If you want I can share a short curl example (erasure request + receipt download) — ping me and I'll paste it in or attach as a gist.
